questions.q: A teacher starts class with yoga, then has writers close their eyes and picture a room in detail before writing in silence. Whose method does this echo?
questions.explain: Warm-up, visualization and silent writing are the best-documented parts of her workshops.

questions.q: What is unusual about the middle part of Fefu and Her Friends?
choices: The audience moves in groups through several spaces where scenes play simultaneously and repeat
questions.explain: Each group sees all four scenes, in different orders.

questions.q: How did Fornés approach structure in her own writing?
choices: Follow characters and images to discover what happens
Outline first, then write scenes to fit
questions.explain: Structure emerged from the work rather than being imposed.

choices: The Hispanic Playwrights-in-Residence Laboratory she led in New York from 1981
questions.explain: It trained a generation of Latinx playwrights, including Nilo Cruz and Migdalia Cruz.

questions.q: Her plays are often built of short scenes, each a sharply framed picture. What's the nearest comparison?
choices: A well-made machine around a secret
A sequence of paintings whose pressure accumulates
questions.explain: She began as a painter, and image is central to her dramaturgy.

questions.q: Why be cautious about any fixed "Fornés system"?
choices: She taught in person and accounts vary; much is passed on by former students
She published a strict manual that's been lost
questions.explain: Her method survives mostly through students' adaptations.

ideas: Close your eyes and see the character in detail before you write a single word.
Begin a writing session with the body: a physical warm-up to quiet the critical mind.
Let the audience walk through the house and assemble the middle of the play in its own order.
